sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sarva ete mahotsāhā ye tvayā parikīrtitāḥ ekatas tv eva te sarve sametā bhīma ekataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: All these warriors of great valor whom you have enumerated — even if all of them were gathered together on one side, Bhīma alone would stand on the other.

sanskrit: bhīmasenād dhi me bhūyo bhayaṃ saṃjāyate mahat kruddhād amarṣaṇāt tāta vyāghrād iva mahāruroḥ
english: My fear of Bhīmasena arises ever greater, Sañjaya — of that enraged, implacable warrior, as of a tiger before a great roebuck.

sanskrit: jāgarmi rātrayaḥ sarvā dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvasan bhīto vṛkodarāt tāta siṃhāt paśur ivābalaḥ
english: I lie awake through all the nights, breathing long hot sighs, afraid of Vṛkodara, dear Sañjaya, as a weak animal is afraid before a lion.

sanskrit: na hi tasya mahābāhoḥ śakrapratimatejasaḥ sainye 'smin pratipaśyāmi ya enaṃ viṣahed yudhi
english: For in this army I see no one equal in might to that mighty-armed one whose splendor rivals Indra's — no one who could withstand him in battle.

sanskrit: amarṣaṇaś ca kaunteyo dṛḍhavairaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ anarmahāsī sonmādas tiryakprekṣī mahāsvanaḥ
english: That son of Kuntī, that Pāṇḍava, is implacable and relentless in enmity — he does not laugh without cause, he seems frenzied, he glances sidelong, and his voice is thunderous.

sanskrit: mahāvego mahotsāho mahābāhur mahābalaḥ mandānāṃ mama putrāṇāṃ yuddhenāntaṃ kariṣyati
english: Of tremendous speed, tremendous energy, mighty-armed, of immense strength — he will bring an end through battle to my foolish sons.

sanskrit: ūrugrāhagṛhītānāṃ gadāṃ bibhrad vṛkodaraḥ kurūṇām ṛṣabho yuddhe daṇḍapāṇir ivāntakaḥ
english: Vṛkodara, bearing the mace seized in the grip of his thighs, stands like Death with rod in hand as the bull among the Kurus in battle.

sanskrit: śaikyāyasamayīṃ ghorāṃ gadāṃ kāñcanabhūṣitām manasāhaṃ prapaśyāmi brahmadaṇḍam ivodyatam
english: In my mind I see that terrible mace of his — made of iron and steel, adorned with gold — raised like the staff of Brahmā.

sanskrit: yathā rurūṇāṃ yūtheṣu siṃho jātabalaś caret māmakeṣu tathā bhīmo baleṣu vicariṣyati
english: As a powerful lion roams among herds of deer, so will Bhīma range through my armies.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ mama putrāṇāṃ sa ekaḥ krūravikramaḥ bahvāśī vipratīpaś ca bālye 'pi rabhasaḥ sadā
english: Of all my sons he alone is of fierce valor — a great eater, contrary and always impetuous even in childhood.

sanskrit: udvepate me hṛdayaṃ yadā duryodhanādayaḥ bālye 'pi tena yudhyanto vāraṇeneva marditāḥ
english: My heart trembles when I recall how even in childhood Duryodhana and the others, fighting against him, were crushed like creatures by an elephant.

sanskrit: tasya vīryeṇa saṃkliṣṭā nityam eva sutā mama sa eva hetur bhedasya bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ
english: My sons have always been tormented by his prowess. He alone — Bhīma of terrible valor — has been the cause of the breach between us.

sanskrit: grasamānam anīkāni naravāraṇavājinām paśyāmīvāgrato bhīmaṃ krodhamūrchitam āhave
english: I seem to see Bhīma before me in battle, swallowing whole the armies of men, elephants, and horses, maddened with rage.

sanskrit: astre droṇārjunasamaṃ vāyuvegasamaṃ jave saṃjayācakṣva me śūraṃ bhīmasenam amarṣaṇam
english: Tell me, Sañjaya, of that hero Bhīmasena the implacable — equal to Droṇa and Arjuna in weaponry, equal to the wind in speed.

sanskrit: atilābhaṃ tu manye 'haṃ yat tena ripughātinā tadaiva na hatāḥ sarve mama putrā manasvinā
english: I count it a great gain that that slayer of enemies, that high-spirited one, did not kill all my sons right then and there.

sanskrit: yena bhīmabalā yakṣā rākṣasāś ca samāhatāḥ kathaṃ tasya raṇe vegaṃ mānuṣaḥ prasahiṣyati
english: He by whose might the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas of great strength were slain — how shall any human withstand his onslaught in battle?

sanskrit: na sa jātu vaśe tasthau mama bālo 'pi saṃjaya kiṃ punar mama duṣputraiḥ kliṣṭaḥ saṃprati pāṇḍavaḥ
english: He never remained under my control even as a child, Sañjaya — how much less now, when he has been wronged and tormented by my wicked sons?

sanskrit: niṣṭhuraḥ sa ca naiṣṭhuryād bhajyed api na saṃnamet tiryakprekṣī saṃhatabhrūḥ kathaṃ śāmyed vṛkodaraḥ
english: Hard and cruel by nature, he would sooner break than bend; with his sidelong glance and knitted brows — how could Vṛkodara ever be pacified?

sanskrit: bṛhadaṃso 'pratibalo gauras tāla ivodgataḥ pramāṇato bhīmasenaḥ prādeśenādhiko 'rjunāt
english: Broad-shouldered, matchless in strength, fair-complexioned, towering like a palm tree — Bhīmasena by measure exceeds Arjuna by a span.

sanskrit: javena vājino 'tyeti balenātyeti kuñjarān avyaktajalpī madhvakṣo madhyamaḥ pāṇḍavo balī
english: In speed he surpasses horses; in strength he surpasses elephants; the middle Pāṇḍava of muted speech, with the eyes of a bee, is immensely powerful.

sanskrit: iti bālye śrutaḥ pūrvaṃ mayā vyāsamukhāt purā rūpato vīryataś caiva yāthātathyena pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Thus did I hear from the mouth of Vyāsa himself in former times of this Pāṇḍava as a child — his form and his valor described truly and accurately.

sanskrit: āyasena sa daṇḍena rathān nāgān hayān narān haniṣyati raṇe kruddho bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: With his iron rod, Bhīma — the foremost of strikers — when enraged will destroy in battle chariots, elephants, horses, and men.

sanskrit: amarṣī nityasaṃrabdho raudraḥ krūraparākramaḥ mama tāta pratīpāni kurvan pūrvaṃ vimānitaḥ
english: Implacable, ever-wrathful, fierce, of terrible valor — he who previously acted against me and was dishonored, dear Sañjaya.

sanskrit: niṣkīrṇām āyasīṃ sthūlāṃ suparvāṃ kāñcanīṃ gadām śataghnīṃ śatanirhrādāṃ kathaṃ śakṣyanti me sutāḥ
english: His mace of iron and steel — massive, well-jointed, gold-adorned, a slayer of hundreds, resounding with a hundred peals — how shall my sons be able to withstand it?

sanskrit: apāram aplavāgādhaṃ samudraṃ śaraveginam bhīmasenamayaṃ durgaṃ tāta mandās titīrṣavaḥ
english: Like a boundless, unfathomable ocean swift as arrows — Bhīmasena is a fortress impossible to breach, dear Sañjaya, yet the fools wish to cross him.

sanskrit: krośato me na śṛṇvanti bālāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ viṣamaṃ nāvabudhyante prapātaṃ madhudarśinaḥ
english: The young fools who fancy themselves wise do not listen even as I cry out; seeing only the honey, they do not perceive the precipice ahead.

sanskrit: saṃyugaṃ ye kariṣyanti nararūpeṇa vāyunā niyataṃ coditā dhātrā siṃheneva mahāmṛgāḥ
english: Those who engage in battle with this Wind in human form are surely urged on by fate — like great deer goaded toward a lion.

sanskrit: śaikyāṃ tāta catuṣkiṣkuṃ ṣaḍasrim amitaujasam prahitāṃ duḥkhasaṃsparśāṃ kathaṃ śakṣyanti me sutāḥ
english: His iron-and-steel mace — four cubits long, six-edged, of immeasurable power, whose touch brings agony — how shall my sons endure its blow, dear Sañjaya?

sanskrit: gadāṃ bhrāmayatas tasya bhindato hastimastakān sṛkkiṇī lelihānasya bāṣpam utsṛjato muhuḥ
english: As he whirls his mace and splits the heads of elephants, licking the corners of his mouth, tears flowing again and again —

sanskrit: uddiśya pātān patataḥ kurvato bhairavān ravān pratīpān patato mattān kuñjarān pratigarjataḥ
english: — charging headlong in aimed attacks, uttering terrible roars, lunging against maddened elephants, roaring back at them —

sanskrit: vigāhya rathamārgeṣu varān uddiśya nighnataḥ agneḥ prajvalitasyeva api mucyeta me prajā
english: — plunging into the chariot lanes and striking down warriors one by one — could my people escape even from blazing fire such as his?

sanskrit: vīthīṃ kurvan mahābāhur drāvayan mama vāhinīm nṛtyann iva gadāpāṇir yugāntaṃ darśayiṣyati
english: That mighty-armed one, clearing a path, routing my army, dancing as it were with mace in hand, will show them the end of an age.

sanskrit: prabhinna iva mātaṅgaḥ prabhañjan puṣpitān drumān pravekṣyati raṇe senāṃ putrāṇāṃ me vṛkodaraḥ
english: Like a rut-maddened elephant breaking flowering trees, Vṛkodara will plunge into the army of my sons in battle.

sanskrit: kurvan rathān vipuruṣān vidhvajān bhagnapuṣkarān ārujan puruṣavyāghro rathinaḥ sādinas tathā
english: That tiger among men will strip the chariots of their warriors and banners and shatter their wheels, and he will tear down chariot-fighters and cavalry alike.

sanskrit: gaṅgāvega ivānūpāṃs tīrajān vividhān drumān pravekṣyati mahāsenāṃ putrāṇāṃ mama saṃjaya
english: As the Ganges' current sweeps down the many diverse trees growing on the marshy banks, so will he plunge into the vast army of my sons, Sañjaya.

sanskrit: vaśaṃ nūnaṃ gamiṣyanti bhīmasenabalārditāḥ mama putrāś ca bhṛtyāś ca rājānaś caiva saṃjaya
english: Surely my sons, my servants, and the kings allied with us will all come under his sway, crushed by the might of Bhīmasena, Sañjaya.

sanskrit: yena rājā mahāvīryaḥ praviśyāntaḥpuraṃ purā vāsudevasahāyena jarāsaṃdho nipātitaḥ
english: He it was who, entering the inner apartments of the palace in former times with Vāsudeva as his ally, brought down Jarāsandha, that king of mighty valor.

sanskrit: kṛtsneyaṃ pṛthivī devī jarāsaṃdhena dhīmatā māgadhendreṇa balinā vaśe kṛtvā pratāpitā
english: The entire earth had been subjugated and oppressed by the wise and powerful king of Magadha, Jarāsandha.

sanskrit: bhīṣmapratāpāt kuravo nayenāndhakavṛṣṇayaḥ te na tasya vaśaṃ jagmuḥ kevalaṃ daivam eva vā
english: The Kurus through Bhīṣma's might, and the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis through policy — they alone did not come under his sway; only fate protected them.

sanskrit: sa gatvā pāṇḍuputreṇa tarasā bāhuśālinā anāyudhena vīreṇa nihataḥ kiṃ tato 'dhikam
english: Yet he was slain by the son of Pāṇḍu — that hero relying only on the strength of his arms, fighting without weapons. What greater feat can there be?

sanskrit: dīrghakālena saṃsiktaṃ viṣam āśīviṣo yathā sa mokṣyati raṇe tejaḥ putreṣu mama saṃjaya
english: Like venom accumulated over a long time in a venomous serpent, he will release his power in battle upon my sons, Sañjaya.

sanskrit: mahendra iva vajreṇa dānavān devasattamaḥ bhīmaseno gadāpāṇiḥ sūdayiṣyati me sutān
english: As the great Indra, best of gods, slays demons with his thunderbolt, so will Bhīmasena with mace in hand destroy my sons.

sanskrit: aviṣahyam anāvāryaṃ tīvravegaparākramam paśyāmīvātitāmrākṣam āpatantaṃ vṛkodaram
english: I seem to see Vṛkodara rushing forward — irresistible, unstoppable, of fierce speed and valor, his eyes blazing copper-red.

sanskrit: agadasyāpy adhanuṣo virathasya vivarmaṇaḥ bāhubhyāṃ yudhyamānasya kas tiṣṭhed agrataḥ pumān
english: Even without a weapon, even without a bow, even dismounted from his chariot, even without armor — fighting with bare arms alone — what man could stand before him?

sanskrit: bhīṣmo droṇaś ca vipro 'yaṃ kṛpaḥ śāradvatas tathā jānanty ete yathaivāhaṃ vīryajñas tasya dhīmataḥ
english: Bhīṣma, Droṇa the brahmin, and Kṛpa son of Śaradvat — they know that wise one's valor just as I, who know valor, know it.

sanskrit: āryavrataṃ tu jānantaḥ saṃgarān na bibhitsavaḥ senāmukheṣu sthāsyanti māmakānāṃ nararṣabhāḥ
english: Yet knowing the code of noble warriors and not wishing to flee from battle, these bulls among men will take their stand at the forefront of my armies.

sanskrit: balīyaḥ sarvato diṣṭaṃ puruṣasya viśeṣataḥ paśyann api jayaṃ teṣāṃ na niyacchāmi yat sutān
english: Fate is mightier than all and specifically mightier than any man — it is because I see that victory is theirs, yet cannot restrain my sons.

sanskrit: te purāṇaṃ maheṣvāsā mārgam aindraṃ samāsthitāḥ tyakṣyanti tumule prāṇān rakṣantaḥ pārthivaṃ yaśaḥ
english: Those great bowmen, taking the ancient path of Indra, will give up their lives in the tumult of battle, protecting their kingly honor.

sanskrit: yathaiṣāṃ māmakās tāta tathaiṣāṃ pāṇḍavā api pautrā bhīṣmasya śiṣyāś ca droṇasya ca kṛpasya ca
english: Just as they are my own people, dear Sañjaya, so equally are the Pāṇḍavas — all are Bhīṣma's grandsons and disciples of Droṇa and Kṛpa.

sanskrit: yat tv asmad āśrayaṃ kiṃ cid dattam iṣṭaṃ ca saṃjaya tasyāpacitim āryatvāt kartāraḥ sthavirās trayaḥ
english: Whatever gifts or honors were bestowed on them from our side, Sañjaya — those three elders out of their nobleness will repay that debt.

sanskrit: ādadānasya śastraṃ hi kṣatradharmaṃ parīpsataḥ nidhanaṃ brāhmaṇasyājau varam evāhur uttamam
english: For one who takes up arms and seeks to uphold the duty of a warrior, death on the battlefield is said to be the highest good — so say even the brahmins.

sanskrit: sa vai śocāmi sarvān vai ye yuyutsanti pāṇḍavān vikruṣṭaṃ vidureṇādau tad etad bhayam āgatam
english: I grieve for all of them — those who fight against the Pāṇḍavas. This very danger that Vidura foretold and cried out against from the beginning has now arrived.

sanskrit: na tu manye vighātāya jñānaṃ duḥkhasya saṃjaya bhavaty atibale hy etaj jñānam apy upaghātakam
english: Yet I do not believe that knowledge avails to ward off suffering, Sañjaya — for in the face of overwhelming power, even knowledge itself becomes destructive.

sanskrit: ṛṣayo hy api nirmuktāḥ paśyanto lokasaṃgrahān sukhe bhavanti sukhinas tathā duḥkhena duḥkhitāḥ
english: Even the sages, though liberated, observing the course of the world, are happy in happiness and pained by pain.

sanskrit: kiṃ punar yo 'ham āsaktas tatra tatra sahasradhā putreṣu rājyadāreṣu pautreṣv api ca bandhuṣu
english: What then of me, who am attached in a thousand ways to sons, to the kingdom and wives, to grandchildren and to kinsmen?

sanskrit: saṃśaye tu mahaty asmin kiṃ nu me kṣamam uttamam vināśaṃ hy eva paśyāmi kurūṇām anucintayan
english: In this great uncertainty, what is the most fitting course for me? For when I reflect, I see nothing but the destruction of the Kurus.

sanskrit: dyūtapramukham ābhāti kurūṇāṃ vyasanaṃ mahat mandenaiśvaryakāmena lobhāt pāpam idaṃ kṛtam
english: The great calamity of the Kurus appears to have begun with the dicing — this evil was done out of greed by one foolishly craving sovereignty.

sanskrit: manye paryāyadharmo 'yaṃ kālasyātyantagāminaḥ cakre pradhir ivāsakto nāsya śakyaṃ palāyitum
english: I believe this is the regular law of Time, which moves to its inexorable end — like the rim fixed to the wheel, there is no fleeing from it.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu kāryaṃ kathaṃ kuryāṃ kva nu gacchāmi saṃjaya ete naśyanti kuravo mandāḥ kālavaśaṃ gatāḥ
english: What is to be done? How should I act? Where shall I go, Sañjaya? These foolish Kurus perish, fallen into the power of Time.

sanskrit: avaśo 'haṃ purā tāta putrāṇāṃ nihate śate śroṣyāmi ninadaṃ strīṇāṃ kathaṃ māṃ maraṇaṃ spṛśet
english: Helpless, when the hundred sons are slain, I will hear the wailing of the women — and then how shall death not touch me?

sanskrit: yathā nidāghe jvalanaḥ samiddho; dahet kakṣaṃ vāyunā codyamānaḥ gadāhastaḥ pāṇḍavas tadvad eva; hantā madīyān sahito 'rjunena
english: As a blazing fire in the summer heat, fanned by the wind, burns through dry grass — just so will that Pāṇḍava with mace in hand, together with Arjuna, be the slayer of my people.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yasya vai nānṛtā vācaḥ pravṛttā anuśuśrumaḥ trailokyam api tasya syād yoddhā yasya dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Of that warrior whose words, we have heard, have never proved false — even the three worlds together could stand as his opponent, if Dhanañjaya were his champion.

sanskrit: tasyaiva ca na paśyāmi yudhi gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ aniśaṃ cintayāno 'pi yaḥ pratīyād rathena tam
english: Even reflecting on it without ceasing, I cannot find any warrior who could face in battle with his chariot the one who wields the Gāṇḍīva bow.

sanskrit: asyataḥ karṇinālīkān mārgaṇān hṛdayacchidaḥ pratyetā na samaḥ kaś cid yudhi gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ
english: As he shoots barbed arrows and reeds and heart-piercing shafts, no equal can be found to face in battle the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: droṇakarṇau pratīyātāṃ yadi vīrau nararṣabhau māhātmyāt saṃśayo loke na tv asti vijayo mama
english: Even if those two heroes among men, Droṇa and Karṇa, were to face him — there might be doubt in the world about the outcome due to their greatness, yet victory is not mine.

sanskrit: ghṛṇī karṇaḥ pramādī ca ācāryaḥ sthaviro guruḥ samartho balavān pārtho dṛḍhadhanvā jitaklamaḥ bhavet sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ sarvaśo 'py aparājayaḥ
english: Karṇa is tender-hearted and negligent; the Teacher is aged and venerable; but the son of Pṛthā is capable, powerful, of the firm bow, and one who has conquered fatigue — the battle will be utterly tumultuous and yet he would remain unvanquished on all sides.

sanskrit: sarve hy astravidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve prāptā mahad yaśaḥ api sarvāmaraiśvaryaṃ tyajeyur na punar jayam vadhe nūnaṃ bhavec chāntis tayor vā phalgunasya vā
english: All are skilled in weapons, all are heroes, all have earned great renown — they would sooner give up the lordship of all the immortals than surrender victory. Only in the death of one of them or of Phalguna would there come peace.

sanskrit: na tu jetārjunasyāsti hantā cāsya na vidyate manyus tasya kathaṃ śāmyen mandān prati ya utthitaḥ
english: Yet Arjuna has no conqueror, and no slayer of him exists; his wrath — how could it be pacified, that wrath which has risen up against fools?

sanskrit: anye 'py astrāṇi jānanti jīyante ca jayanti ca ekāntavijayas tv eva śrūyate phalgunasya ha
english: Others too know the weapons — they are sometimes defeated, sometimes victorious — but of Phalguna alone is absolute and undivided victory spoken.

sanskrit: trayastriṃśat samāhūya khāṇḍave 'gnim atarpayat jigāya ca surān sarvān nāsya vedmi parājayam
english: He summoned the thirty-three gods and satisfied the fire at Khandava; he conquered all the gods — I know of no defeat of his.

sanskrit: yasya yantā hṛṣīkeśaḥ śīlavṛttasamo yudhi dhruvas tasya jayas tāta yathendrasya jayas tathā
english: He whose charioteer is Hrishikesha, equal in character and conduct in battle — his victory is certain, dear Sañjaya, as is the victory of Indra himself.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇāv ekarathe yattāv adhijyaṃ gāṇḍivaṃ dhanuḥ yugapat trīṇi tejāṃsi sametāny anuśuśrumaḥ
english: The two Kṛṣṇas straining together on one chariot, and the Gāṇḍīva bow with its string drawn — we have heard that three blazing splendors are united in one.

sanskrit: naiva no 'sti dhanus tādṛṅ na yoddhā na ca sārathiḥ tac ca mandā na jānanti duryodhanavaśānugāḥ
english: We have no such bow, no such warrior, and no such charioteer — and this the fools who follow Duryodhana do not know.

sanskrit: śeṣayed aśanir dīpto nipatan mūrdhni saṃjaya na tu śeṣaṃ śarāḥ kuryur astās tāta kirīṭinā
english: A blazing thunderbolt falling on the head would leave something behind, Sañjaya — but the arrows shot by the Diademed one would leave nothing at all.

sanskrit: api cāsyann ivābhāti nighnann iva ca phalgunaḥ uddharann iva kāyebhyaḥ śirāṃsi śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: I seem to see Phalguna shooting, striking, tearing heads from bodies with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: api bāṇamayaṃ tejaḥ pradīptam iva sarvataḥ gāṇḍīveddhaṃ dahetājau putrāṇāṃ mama vāhinīm
english: I seem to see a blazing fire of arrows lit everywhere by the Gāṇḍīva, burning the army of my sons on the battlefield.

sanskrit: api sā rathaghoṣeṇa bhayārtā savyasācinaḥ vitrastā bahulā senā bhāratī pratibhāti me
english: I seem to see that great Bharata army, terrified by the thunder of Savyasācin's chariot, trembling and overwhelmed with fear.

sanskrit: yathā kakṣaṃ dahaty agniḥ pravṛddhaḥ sarvataś caran mahārcir aniloddhūtas tadvad dhakṣyati māmakān
english: As a fire blazing and ranging everywhere with its great flames, fanned by the wind, burns through dry grass — so will he burn my people.

sanskrit: yadodvaman niśitān bāṇasaṃghān; sthātātatāyī samare kirīṭī sṛṣṭo 'ntakaḥ sarvaharo vidhātrā; yathā bhavet tadvad avāraṇīyaḥ
english: When the Diademed one, standing firm as a relentless aggressor in battle, vomits forth his showers of sharp arrows — like Death the all-destroyer as fashioned by the Creator — he will be utterly unstoppable.

sanskrit: yadā hy abhīkṣṇaṃ subahūn prakārāñ; śrotāsmi tān āvasathe kurūṇām teṣāṃ samantāc ca tathā raṇāgre; kṣayaḥ kilāyaṃ bharatān upaiti
english: For when I repeatedly hear of those many diverse deeds in the dwelling place of the Kurus, and of their destruction on all sides and at the front of battle — then surely this annihilation comes upon the Bharatas.
